t: A Saharan kingdom in Libya's Fezzan, sustained by underground foggara channels tapping fossil water beneath the desert.
It controlled trans-Saharan routes, sending ivory, enslaved people and wild animals to Carthaginian and Roman markets.
As the water table sank below the channels and trade faltered, it faded into scattered oases before the Arab conquest.
dyk: In the Wadi al-Ajal alone the Garamantes dug an estimated 550 or more foggara channels with over 100,000 vertical shafts to bring water to their fields.
ev: Lucius Cornelius Balbus captures Garama, earning Rome's last triumph for a non-imperial general
The Garamantes join Oea against Leptis Magna and are driven back by Valerius Festus
Septimius Severus campaigns against the Garamantes and sets outposts at Ghadames and Bu Njem
The Vandal conquest of North Africa begins, disrupting Mediterranean trade demand
Garama is greatly reduced as falling groundwater starves the foggara system
Arab expeditions into the Fezzan begin, meeting little significant resistance
